messages.subject: Using the procD.lm
parts:
Hello, 

I have some problems figuring out if I am using the ProCD.lm function correctly and getting the right out of it. 

I am testing whether there are any size and shape differences between males and females in one population of animals. I have microscribed 31 landmarks on the skulls, and converted them to a TPS format, and used the readland.tps to put the data into R: 

mydata <- readland.tps("Skulls", specID ="ID")

I added a separate document containing one column with the IDs and one with the ID "Sex" telling if they are female or male. 

classifier <- read.csv("Classifier.csv", header=TRUE, row.name=1, sep="\t")  

I did a GPA:
  
gpa <- gpagen(mydata, PrinAxes = TRUE, ProcD = TRUE, Proj = TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)

And a PCA:
 
gp <- interaction(classifier$Sex) 
PCA_skulls <- plotTangentSpace(gpa$coords, groups = gp)


Then I wanted to test if males and females are different in size or shape.
I made a dataframe:

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape=gpa$coords, size=gpa$Csize, sex=classifier$Sex)

And from here I start questioning myself if I am during it correctly. I am using the proCD.lm function. 

I took the size and shape separately:

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(shape=gpa$coords, size=gpa$Csize, sex=classifier$Sex) 
 
myresults<-procD.lm(shape~sex, data = gdf)
myresults2<-procD.lm(size~sex, data = gdf)

And got this for shape:
procD.lm(f1 = shape ~ sex, data = gdf)

Type I (Sequential) Sums of Squares and Cross-products
Randomized Residual Permutation Procedure Used
1000 Permutations
ANOVA effect sizes and P-values based on empirical F distributions

sex           1    0.08868 0.088681 0.25081 25.443 5.9886  0.001 **
Residuals 76  0.26490 0.003485 0.74919                        
Total         77  0.35358                                         
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 

And this for size:
procD.lm(f1 = size ~ sex, data = gdf)

Type I (Sequential) Sums of Squares and Cross-products
Randomized Residual Permutation Procedure Used
1000 Permutations
ANOVA effect sizes and P-values based on empirical F distributions

                  Df     SS          MS     Rsq            F         Z        Pr(>F)   
sex            1    145084 145084 0.75485    234.01 3.0314  0.001 **
Residuals 76   47119    620       0.24515                        
Total           77 192204                                       
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1


However, I do not know if this is the correct way of during it, or if I should have the size and shape into one equation? And if it actually is testing whether females and males are different?

Thanks,

Julie

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Using the procD.lm
parts:
Julie,

 

Yes, your use of procD.lm has resulted in a comparison of males and females for their size, and then for their shape. Other analyses are possible (see help files for examples), but to answer your question: yes, you have compared male vs. female size and shape.

 

Best,


Dean
